The instant appeal has bee filed by the Insurance Company challenging the order passed in E.C.No.66 of 2017 on the file of the Commissioner for Employees Compensation and Joint Commissioner of Labour, Trichirappalli primarily on the ground of liability.

(A)Factual Matrix:
2.According to the claimants, the deceased Nagesh @ Kandasamy was a lorry driver and he was working under the first opposite party in the claim petition.
According to them, the deceased had driven the vehicle from Gujarat to Theni with mustard load and it reached Theni at 6.00 a.m on 03.10.2012.
He had parked the lorry at Kathiresan lorry office.
The deceased was waiting in the lorry office for loading.
While the deceased was going to attend nature call in the earlier morning on 04.10.2012, he had slipped and fallen on the road.
He sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
3.According to the claimants, the accident has taken place during the course of employment and they are entitled to a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.

4.The Insurance Company had filed a counter contending that the deceased was not working under the first respondent and there is no employer employee relationship.
That apart, the accident has not happened in the course of employment.
The have further contended that there is no nexus between the death of the alleged employee and the employment and therefore, the principle of notional extension cannot be invoked.
They have further stated that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol as elucidated in the F.I.R and therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation.

5.The Commissioner for Employees Compensation after considering the oral and documentary evidence filed on either side had arrived at a finding that the deceased was an assistant driver under the first respondent and therefore, there is employer and employee relationship between the deceased and the first respondent.

The Commissioner had further found that when the deceased was waiting for the next load in the lorry office, while he had moved for attending nature calls, he had M/S Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Elammal on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171113468/

The Commissioner had fixed a sum of Rs.6784/- as monthly salary based upon the minimum wages fixed by the Government of Tamil Nadu and ultimately,
arrived at a compensation of Rs.6,38,965/- along https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis with interest at the rate of 12% from the date of the accident.
This award is under challenge in the present appeal by the insurance company.

(B).Contentions of the Counsels:
6.The
learned counsel for the appellant herein had contended that the deceased had reached the destination namely Theni at 6.00 a.m on 03.10.2012.
However, the death is said to have taken place in the early morning hours on 04.10.2012.
Therefore, there is no nexus between the death and the employment.
He had further contended that the death has not arisen due to the involvement of the motor vehicle.
The deceased had moved in an inebriated mood to attend the nature call and he had fallen down and passed away.
Therefore, the said death cannot be considered to be a motor accident.

7.The learned counsel for the appellant had further contended that the claimants have not established the fact that the deceased was employed under the first respondent and there was an employer employee relationship.
The appeal had been filed raising the substantial questions of law on the above said issue.

8.Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondents herein had contended that the appellant/insurance company has not deposited the entire award amount along with interest and therefore, the appeal is not https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis maintainable.
He relied upon the Judgement of our High Court reported in 2015 (1) TN MAC 734 (C.Arumugham @ Raj Vs. Revathi and others).

11.It is the specific contention of the claimants that the deceased had driven the vehicle from Gujarat to Theni and reached the destination at 6.00 a.m on 03.10.2012.

sentences.text: During the early morning on 04.10.2012, when he had gone to attend the nature call, he had slipped, sustained head injury and passed away.
Therefore, according to the claimants, the accident has taken place in the course of employment.
The claimants have examined the first respondent who is not only the owner of the lorry, but also the co-driver who had accompanied the deceased from Gujarat to Theni.
12.The
owner of the lorry had lodged the F.I.R before the police and the same is marked as Exhibit P1.
A perusal of the said F.I.R reveals that the deceased was working as an assistant driver under him.

When the owner of the lorry himself has lodged a police complaint admitting the fact that the deceased was the driver employed under him, the contention of the appellant/insurance company that the employer employee relationship has not been established is not legally sustainable.

13.It has been further contended on the side of the claimants that while waiting for the next load, the deceased had fallen down, sustained head injury https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and passed away.
The fact that the deceased was staying in the lorry shed in the night of 03.10.2012 awaiting the next load after unloading the goods is not disputed by the Insurance Company.
The said fact is also borne out of the F.I.R registered by the owner of the lorry under Exhibit P1.
Therefore, the Joint Commissioner of Labour was right in invoking the principles of notional extension of employment and found that the said accident has taken place during the course of employment.

14.The learned counsel for the respondents had contended that the present appeal filed by the Insurance Company is not maintainable in view of the fact that the entire award amount has not been deposited along with interest.
However, a perusal of the record indicates that the entire award along with interest has been deposited before the Commissioner and only thereafter, the present appeal has been filed.
Therefore, the contention of the learned counsel appearing for the respondents touching upon the maintainability is not legally sustainable.

15.The employer employee relationship and the fact that the accident has taken place during the course of employment have been established by the claimants and therefore, all the substantial questions of law are answered as against the appellant.
There are no merits in the appeal and this Civil https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Miscellaneous Appeal stands dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
